info.title: Embedding Atlas data API
info.summary: Keyless, CORS-open JSON and CSV over public water, trade, jobs, housing, hazard and land sources, with provenance on every number.
info.description: Every JSON response is an envelope: route-specific fields at the top level, the payload in `data`, one `provenance` record per upstream release the numbers came from (estimates carry their formula in `method`), and `generatedAt`. Tabular ops answer `format=csv` with the same provenance as `#` comment lines after the data. See docs/API.md for citation format, caching, courtesy and per-source revision caveats.

get.summary: The catalogue: every curated collection eye draws or reads, with what a record is, its sources and licences, coverage, freshness, what is excluded and why, caveats and the ops that serve it
get.description: Static (bundled with the app, no upstream call). Each collection names its layer, its sources (expanded from the source registry: name, publisher, url, licence), what one record means and does not mean, spatial and temporal coverage with a dated count where one was taken, freshness as the upstream states it with the field it was read from and the date it was read, exclusions with the reason for each, caveats, the fields that may be searched and the fields safe to embed (never an address, contact or a name that can be a person's), and its ops as `route?op=x`. Listed for people at /catalog. `uncatalogued` names the layers with no entry yet. op=search ranks the collections by meaning: the query (2-200 characters) is embedded with potion-base-8M and compared with each card's own description (cosine, 4 decimals); collections only, records are searched by meaning in the browser palette. op=place-export returns a committed per-county aggregate with its provenance (query, page sha256s, fetch time), zero-vs-missing and null rules and join checks: npl-status (NPL sites per county and year, 2015-2025, form series), ust-releases-county and ust-facilities-county (EPA UST Finder county counts of releases and of facilities and tanks, 2018-2021 state records, form static; the release layer never publishes a 0 for open or no-further-action counts, so a null there most likely means 0 for many counties, kept null and not random: meta.nullCellNote) and fuds-properties (USACE FUDS properties per county, FY2024 inventory, form static; a 0 means no property USACE locates in the county, an approved rule, with the strict alternative in meta.counts.strictRule for reference). Every export's meta.form is present in the response.

op=search.weights: /embed/potion-base-8M-bf8b0566/ (int8 table, per-row scales, vocab, manifest.json with sha256s, LICENSE)

op=place-export.npl-status: lib/catalog/data/npl-county.json (scripts/export-npl-county.mjs); source EPA Superfund NPL Sites with Status Information FeatureServer/0
op=place-export.ust-releases-county: lib/catalog/data/ust-releases-county.json (scripts/export-ust-county.mjs); source EPA UST Finder FeatureServer/3 Releases_by_County
op=place-export.ust-facilities-county: lib/catalog/data/ust-facilities-county.json (scripts/export-ust-county.mjs); source EPA UST Finder FeatureServer/2 Facilities_by_County
op=place-export.fuds-properties: lib/catalog/data/fuds-county.json (scripts/export-fuds-county.mjs); source USACE FUDS FeatureServer/1 property points, joined with TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Counties 500K

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: One collection, e.g. nrhp-listed. An unknown id answers 404 with the list of ids in `details.ids`.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: A layer id, e.g. crithab: that layer's collections (an empty list for a layer not yet catalogued; 400 for an id that is not a layer).

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: search: collections ranked by meaning (needs q). place-export: a committed per-county aggregate (needs collection). Omit for the catalogue itself.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: op=search: the query text. 400 outside 2-200 characters.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: op=search: how many collections.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: op=place-export: which aggregate.

200.description: The envelope; `data.collections` (or `data.collection` with id=). op=search: `data.hits` [{ id, title, layer, score, ops, catalog }], `data.embedder` { id, model, commit, tableSha256, licence } and `data.matched` (false when no word of the query is in the model's vocabulary; hits is then empty). op=place-export: `data` { meta, places, value, nullPlaces, ... }; meta.form is always present: series gives value[place][year][feature] over meta.years (npl-status, with siteIds); meta.form static gives value[place][feature] for one snapshot (meta.asOf, meta.years null), with nullCells (UST: a field the layer leaves null) and sourceIds (UST OBJECTIDs) or propertyIds (FUDS).

get.summary: Trade, commerce and real-estate ops
get.description: One route, dispatched on `op`. Bounding boxes are clamped to 18° and snapped outward to a 1° grid so nearby callers share a cache entry. Tabular ops (`areas`, `sectors`, `ports`, `border`, `countries`, `pulse`) accept `format=csv`. The occupation ops (`msas`, `msa-jobs`) read a bundled BLS OEWS release, so they answer without an upstream call.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: areas: counties in a bbox (or every state with level=state) joined with QCEW jobs/wages and Zillow home values/rents. sectors: NAICS sector mix for a county (SSCCC) or state (SS000) with location quotients. msas: every metropolitan statistical area with its centroid, employment and most distinctive occupation group. msa-jobs: the occupation mix of one MSA (top 30 detailed occupations and all 22 SOC major groups, with wages and location quotients). context: sector mix plus metro, state and US home values. ports: World Port Index harbours in a bbox with BTS Port Performance volumes. border: every US land port of entry with 25 months of BTS counts. countries: Natural Earth polygons with World Bank GDP, exports, imports, trade/GDP, TEU. partners: top trading partners (WITS). pulse: national FRED and BTS series. report: the market report for a point.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: `w,s,e,n` degrees. Required for op=areas (level=county) and op=ports.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: op=areas: county polygons in the bbox, or every state.

parameters.name: fips
parameters.description: op=sectors, op=context: county GEOID (48453) or state (48000).

parameters.name: msa
parameters.description: op=msa-jobs: 5-digit CBSA code (41700). `data` is null with a caveat when the release has no such MSA.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: op=ports: smallest harbour size to include; any harbour with BTS statistics is always included.

parameters.name: iso3
parameters.description: op=partners: reporter country.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: op=pulse with format=csv: long format, one row per observation instead of one per series.

get.summary: Water ops
get.description: One route, dispatched on `op`. Bounding boxes are clamped to 4° and snapped outward to a 0.5° grid. Tabular ops (`gauges`, `wells`, `nwps`, `twdb`, `history`, `matchup`) accept `format=csv`.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: gauges: USGS latest continuous readings in a bbox (flow, stage, temperature, DO, conductance, pH, turbidity, reservoir elevation/storage). wells: USGS latest daily groundwater levels with aquifer names. nwps: NOAA NWPS gauges with flood categories. twdb: Texas reservoirs. drought: US Drought Monitor current polygons. history: 365 days of daily means for one site and parameter. matchup: instantaneous values for one site and parameter in a window. normals: USGS daily-mean discharge percentiles (5th to 95th) for a calendar day, per site (sites=, date=MM-DD). impaired: EPA ATTAINS assessment units states report as impaired (303(d)), lines and areas, in a box clamped to 0.12 degrees and snapped to 0.02 (not the 4 degree water box): category with its meaning, 303(d) listing and TMDL (null when not reported, never N), reporting cycle, overall status, EPA action status verbatim and the How's My Waterway link; 2,000 per layer; `coverage` says per layer whether it answered (a failed layer has count null: unknown, not none). A listing for the whole unit and one cycle, not a measurement; waters not returned were not reported impaired, which includes waters never assessed. pfas: PFAS in public drinking water, EPA UCMR 5 (2023-2025), for the water systems serving a box clamped to 0.12 degrees and snapped to 0.02: systems found by EPA's community water system service areas first, then by EPA's estimated location; each system detected, not-detected, not-in-ucmr5 or unknown, with the highest single result per PFAS in ng/L (never compared with a health limit); service-area polygons only with polygons=1. Samples are taken where treated water enters the distribution system, not at a tap. report: the community water report for a point. reach: the NHDPlus V2 reach a point (lon, lat; snapped to 0.001 degrees) drains to: USGS NLDI's catchment containing the point (comid), then EPA's NHDPlus V2.1 attributes by comid (GNIS name, NHD feature type, Strahler order, total drainage area km², modelled mean annual flow in cfs as EROM gauge-adjusted QE_MA and runoff-only QA_MA). A point with no catchment (ocean, outside the network) answers 200 with comid null; -9999 and missing values are null, never 0; flows are model output, not measurements. trace: one NLDI navigation from a reach (comid from op=reach): mode=down the main stem downstream as a MultiLineString (distance default 100 km), mode=gauges the USGS stream gauges upstream as Points (default 150 km), mode=basin the drainage basin as one polygon (NLDI's simplified basin, at most 2,000 vertices; to fit, holes and islands below an area that grows with the cut are left out and counted in droppedRings, droppedUnderKm2: a dropped hole adds ground that does not drain there, a dropped island leaves out ground that does); distance is always sent and capped at 500 km. A river path on the NHDPlus V2 network, not the HUC-12 chain of /api/fabric?op=downstream.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: `w,s,e,n` degrees. Required for op=gauges, wells, nwps, impaired, pfas.

parameters.name: polygons
parameters.description: op=pfas: draw each system on its service-area polygon (the globe asks below 10 km); without it, systems are points at EPA's estimated location.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: USGS parameter code(s). op=gauges: optional comma list to narrow; op=history, op=matchup: one code, required.

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: op=history, op=matchup: monitoring location id.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: op=matchup: window start, ISO 8601 with Z.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: op=matchup: window end, ISO 8601 with Z.

parameters.name: sites
parameters.description: op=normals: comma list of up to 200 USGS site numbers (with or without USGS-).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: op=normals: MM-DD, the calendar day; today (UTC) when omitted.

parameters.name: comid
parameters.description: op=trace: NHDPlus V2 comid, from op=reach (e.g. 23398863, the Boise River at Boise).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: op=trace: down (main stem downstream), basin (drainage basin), gauges (USGS stream gauges upstream).

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: op=trace with mode=down or gauges: km of channel to navigate (default 100 for down, 150 for gauges; at most 500). The gauge count depends on it.

get.summary: The constructs at a point, one kind of construct across a box, where a point's water goes, what drains to it, or how two places compare
get.description: The place fabric: the human and scientific frames laid over one point. US points get Census TIGERweb units (state, county, incorporated place or CDP, tract, ZCTA, school districts, congressional and state legislative districts, metro/micro area, CSA, urban area, tribal land, census division and region), USGS WBD hydrologic units HUC-2 to HUC-12 with the downstream HUC-12, EPA level III/IV ecoregions, FEMA NFHL flood zone, NFIP community and FIRM panel, the NWS forecast office, forecast zone and time zone, USGS 3DEP elevation, and the EPA region, FEMA region and Federal Reserve district from published lists (split Reserve-district states are named as split). Anywhere, the Natural Earth country and continent. `edges` carry only relations the unit systems define (`nests-in`: GEOID and HUC nesting, OMB metro delineation) or an agency publishes (`assigned-to`: NWS zone to office, state to federal region; `drains-to`: WBD ToHUC). An upstream that fails is listed in `data.failed` and in `caveats`; the call still answers. The point is snapped to a 0.001 degree grid and cached six hours. op=field returns every unit of one kind inside a bbox (kind, or pov + h for the kind that emerges at a camera height), clamped per kind. op=downstream walks WBD ToHUC from the HUC-12 under a point; WBD answers cold queries slowly, so each call stops at a time budget and returns `next`, and op=downstream&from=<next> continues. op=outlines returns outlines and centroids for the chain in batches. op=upstream reads the bundled national ToHUC table backwards: every HUC-12 that drains to the outlet of the subwatershed under a point, compacted to the smallest cover of whole WBD units (level 2 to 12 digits). op=units returns names, published areas and (unless geometry=0) generalised outlines for WBD units of any level. op=compare takes two points (lon, lat and lon2, lat2) and answers which constructs they share (same unit), differ on (both have the kind, different units) or only one has, with a one-line summary such as "same county, different congressional district" and a globe link that opens the comparison.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: stack: the constructs at a point. field: every unit of one kind in a bbox. downstream: one time-boxed leg of the HUC-12 chain from a point (or `from` a HUC-12) toward its terminal. outlines: generalised outlines and centroids for up to 100 HUC-12s. upstream: the catchment of the HUC-12 under a point (or huc12=), as a cover of whole WBD units. units: names, areas and outlines for WBD units of any level (codes=, up to 100; geometry=0 for up to 500 without outlines). compare: which constructs two points share and where they differ.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude of the point, degrees. Required for op=stack, op=downstream and op=compare (point A).

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude of the point, degrees. Required for op=stack, op=downstream and op=compare (point A).

parameters.name: lon2
parameters.description: op=compare: longitude of point B, degrees.

parameters.name: lat2
parameters.description: op=compare: latitude of point B, degrees.

parameters.name: geometry
parameters.description: op=stack: 1 adds each construct's generalised outline as `rings`. For op=units, geometry=0 returns names and areas only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: op=downstream: continue a truncated walk from this HUC-12 (a previous leg's `next`).

parameters.name: huc12
parameters.description: op=outlines: comma list of 1 to 100 twelve-digit HUC-12 codes.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: op=field: west,south,east,north in degrees; clamped to the kind's widest span and snapped to a grid.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: op=field: the construct kind to tile the box with.

parameters.name: pov
parameters.description: op=field without kind: the point of view whose kind emerges at height h.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: op=field with pov: camera height in metres.

parameters.name: codes

get.summary: Current wildfires, the last 24 hours of satellite fire detections, and hazard alerts; USFS Wildfire Risk to Communities ranks; county hazard history (FEMA declarations, USDM drought, NOAA climate, SPC tornadoes, USGS landslide susceptibility)
get.description: op=wildfire: every current US wildland fire from NIFC WFIGS, as perimeters (acres, percent contained, discovery date, the perimeter's capture time; `perimeter captured` says "not published by WFIGS" where it has none rather than borrowing the record's edit time) and incident points for fires with no perimeter yet. op=fires: NASA FIRMS hotspots of the last 24 hours (VIIRS S-NPP, VIIRS NOAA-20, MODIS) inside `bbox` as rows (see `columns`); over `max` they are binned to a square grid and each cell keeps its brightest detection (max FRP) with the count it stands for. Confidence stays on each instrument's scale (VIIRS low / nominal / high, MODIS 0-100 %). op=alerts: every active NWS alert (the polygon NWS published, or else the counties its SAME codes list, dashed on the globe), every GDACS event marked current (RSS, EVENTS4APP and a SEARCH for current Orange and Red events, merged), and NASA EONET open volcano events; severities as each publisher gives them, unrated as "not rated by source". GDACS quakes the USGS 24 h feed also has carry `alsoInUsgs`, and NWS alerts the live feed behind /api/live outlined carry `liveOutlined` (read from the same five-minute cache entry, within the same 20 s budget; when that feed failed or was late none is marked and `counts.nws.liveChecked` is false); none is dropped. Each alerts source gets 20 s; one that does not answer is named in `failed` and in `caveats`. Not a warning service. op=wrc: USDA Forest Service Wildfire Risk to Communities, 2nd edition (2024; LANDFIRE 2020 fuels; boundaries May 2025 from TIGER 2023), CC0 1.0. Four rank families by the service's own aliases (RISK_NATIONAL_RANK, BP_NATIONAL_RANK, WHP_NATIONAL_RANK, EA_HURISK_NATIONAL_RANK, and their _STATE_ ranks); the service does not say which of RISK_* and EA_HURISK_* is wildfirerisk.org's 'Risk to Homes'. Ranks are published as percent strings ('97.20%'); here they are numbers 0-100 with the strings kept in `raw`, and a blank (' ', DC and the 484 excluded communities) is null, never 0. level=county: every county's ranks, exposure shares and building and housing-unit counts, attributes only (two pages of 2,000, held a week); join by `geoid` onto county outlines (Connecticut in planning regions). level=place&bbox=: WRC's community (Census place) polygons in a box of at most 1 degree snapped to 0.05, at most 1,000, with exclude and exclude_re as published. level=fips&fips=: one county (5 digits) or community (7 digits); 404 when WRC has no row. Modelled relative ranks: not a forecast, not a local assessment. op=history: one county's hazard history (fips=<5 digits>, or lon and lat for the county containing the point, from TIGERweb's 1:20M counties). data.series[] are lib/series Series ({ id, title, unit, frequency, geo, provenance, points: [{ t: epoch ms, v }] }): fema:dr:<fips>, fema:em:<fips> and fema:fm:<fips> (FEMA OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries v2: distinct disasterNumber per year of declarationDate, by declaration type, never blended); usdm:dsci:<fips> (the U.S. Drought Monitor's weekly Drought Severity and Coverage Index, 0-500, since 2000, t = mapDate); cag:tavg:<fips> and cag:pcp:<fips> (NOAA NCEI Climate at a Glance annual average temperature, F, and precipitation, in, since 1895; Alaska from 1925, Hawaii from 1991, none for Puerto Rico); spc:tornadoes:<fips> (NOAA SPC tornado rows naming the county per year, 1950-2025, baked from SPC's file). data.declarations[]: FEMA's rows newest first (disasterNumber, declarationType, declarationDate, incidentType, declarationTitle verbatim, incident dates, programs IH/IA/PA/HM, designatedArea verbatim), at most `declarations`; data.declarationRows counts them all. data.droughtNow: the newest week's categorical D0-D4 area shares (statisticsType=2). data.landslide: USGS's county row (prop_susc, susc_area and county_area in km2, v2_ls_count, v2_density) or null. data.missing[]: { source, reason } for every part with none: join:legacy_ct_counties (Connecticut's planning regions get drought only: FEMA, NOAA, SPC and USGS publish the legacy counties), join:boundary_changed_since_2010, source:not_in_release, source:not_published_for_puerto_rico or source:failed (unknown, not empty; a caveat says so). A year with no FEMA declaration or SPC tornado is absent, not 0, until the zero rule is decided (meta.zeroFill). meta.notCounty and meta.unmatched count FEMA rows that name no current county. part=landslide answers { fips, name, state, landslide, missing } from the bake alone. Round 8: se:<type>:<fips> series (se:hail, se:thunderstorm-wind, se:flash-flood and every other type with a report in the county) are NOAA NCEI Storm Events county-coded reports per year by event type since 1996, baked from NCEI's 31 details files into per-state shards (one loaded per call): a row counts when it is county-coded (CZ_TYPE C), not a Tornado (SPC's record owns tornadoes) and its county code and CZ_NAME agree with the county; zone-coded rows are never attached. A type's year is a null point (data.storms.types[].blank, reason zone-coded) where 10 % or more of its reports nationally were zone-coded, never 0. data.storms: { fips, years: [first, last], lastYearMonth, types: [{ type, points: [[year, reports]], blank: [[year, 'zone-coded']], total }], break: { year, what } | null, zeroFill } or null; missing reasons add join:ncei_areas_not_counties (Alaska: NCEI's Alaska rows are its own areas). part=storms answers { fips, name, state, series, storms, missing } from the bake alone, with no upstream. One upstream failing is a caveat, never a 500; 404 for a FIPS that is not a current county.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: wildfire: NIFC WFIGS perimeters and incident points (US). fires: NASA FIRMS 24 h hotspots in a bbox. alerts: NWS + GDACS + EONET. nri: FEMA National Risk Index, December 2025, as FEMA publishes it: composite risk score and rating, expected annual loss (EAL_VALT, dollars a year) and its rating, social vulnerability (SOVI_*, which FEMA says comes from the Census Community Resilience Estimate, not CDC SVI) and community resilience (RESL_*), and the 18 hazard ratings (*_RISKR). level=county (default; the box is snapped as op=areas snaps it, at most 18 degrees on a 1 degree grid): attribute rows only, to join by STCOFIPS onto county outlines (Connecticut in planning regions 09110-09190). level=tract (box at most 0.4 degrees, snapped to 0.05, around the box's centre): NRI's tract polygons as GeoJSON, paged by 2,000, at most two pages (dense 0.4 degree boxes over New York City hold 2,544 to 2,884 tracts and take both pages). Ratings are verbatim; Not Applicable, Insufficient Data, No Rating and Data Unavailable are not a class. A relative index (a percentile among all counties, or all tracts), not a likelihood; county and tract scores are not comparable. op=nri&fips=: one county (5 digits, by STCOFIPS) or tract (11 digits, by TRACTFIPS) with the same named fields and no geometry, `data: { level, fips, row }`; 404 'not in the index' when FEMA has no row (for a click answer and the MCP social_vulnerability pairing). wrc: USFS Wildfire Risk to Communities ranks (county, community polygons, or one GEOID). history: one county's hazard history (FEMA declarations, USDM drought, NOAA climate, SPC tornadoes, USGS landslide susceptibility).

get.summary: Flood zones, wetlands, historic places, public and protected lands in a box, or the ground elevation or critical habitat at a point; BIA trust land (Land Area Representation)
get.description: op=flood: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer flood hazard zones (layer 28) with FEMA's meaning of each zone, whether the ground is in the special flood hazard area, and the base flood elevation where FEMA published one (the -9999 sentinel is dropped). A regulatory map, not a forecast; a box with no zone is not a finding of no risk. Boxes are clamped to 0.08° and snapped to a 0.02° grid. op=wetlands: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory polygons with their Cowardin code, type, acres, the system, class and water regime names decoded locally from the Cowardin code (a part not recognised stays absent), and the year of the imagery each was mapped from (`imageYears`, null when NWI's source layer did not answer); same box rules, at most 500 polygons a query. op=historic: National Register of Historic Places listings as NPS's public spatial data publishes them (STATUS 'Listed', and never a record whose Address NPS marks restricted, which a few boundary records still carry; Address itself is never requested): NRIS number, the property's name as NPS lists it (it can include a person's name; it is not a search key), resource type, National Historic Landmark flag, listing date (NPS's partial CertDate, e.g. 2007-10), city, county, state and the National Archives nomination link. Points always; with polygons=1 the district and site boundaries too. No street address is requested. Archaeological sites whose locations are restricted under NHPA section 304 / ARPA are not in NPS's public data, so absence is not absence on the ground, and this is not a Section 106 review. Boxes are clamped to 0.12° and snapped to 0.02°; at most 2,000 per layer. op=crithab: the USFWS designated critical habitat, final (`final`) and proposed (`proposed`), that contains lon, lat: species common and scientific name, listing status, whether the designation is Final or Proposed, the Federal Register citation and its publication date. FWS's placeholder text ("Please check current species specific shapefile") is read as no value. And NOAA Fisheries critical habitat for marine and anadromous species (`noaa`): polygons of layer 226 containing the point and river and stream lines of layer 2 within about 200 m (a box 0.002 degrees each way), with agency, shape, listing, Final or Proposed, unit, the Federal Register citation split from NOAA's HTML anchor, eCFR section and dates; null when NOAA did not answer (unknown, not absent). And `ranges`: the listed and proposed species whose range covers the point, from EPA OPP's Species_Ranges layer 3 (distinct values, never drawn), with listing status, entity, lead agency, taxonomic group, range date and ECOS link; a range is not presence; null when that layer did not answer. A layer that did not answer is null (unknown, not absent). Regulatory designations, not range or occurrence; FWS says its GIS files are not the legal boundary; NOAA Fisheries' marine and anadromous species are not included. op=publiclands: USGS PAD-US 4.1 fee, easement, designation and proclamation areas with owner, manager, local owner, easement holder, public access, GAP status and IUCN category as PAD-US publishes them; boxes up to 2°, snapped to 0.25°; a box taller than 1.5° keeps the largest 600 units, generalised. op=elevation: USGS 3DEP ground elevation (EPQS) in metres with the source DEM resolution; outside 3DEP coverage `metres` is absent and `note` carries what EPQS said. Only the returned `bbox` is loaded. op=tribal: the Bureau of Indian Affairs' American Indian and Alaska Native Land Area Representation (US federal work): the outer extent of land held in trust or restricted fee for federally recognized tribes and individual Indians, 335 land areas in one national GeoJSON answer simplified to 0.01 degrees (held a day), each with LARID, region, CLASSIFICATION as BIA codes it (no published meaning), GIS acres, BIA's reference-only sentence and a link to BIA's page. Polygon parts under 0.7 km2 (allotment-sized) are dropped before the answer leaves the server, each land area's largest part kept; meta.droppedParts counts them and meta.hiddenAreas lists any land area with nothing drawn. BIA's layer has no Eastern Oklahoma region rows and no Oklahoma land, and not every tribe's land, so a blank area does not mean no tribal land. For illustrative and reference purposes only; never a statement about jurisdiction. No bbox and no detail level.

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: flood: FEMA NFHL zones. wetlands: USFWS NWI polygons with imagery years. historic (nhl=1 for National Historic Landmarks only): NPS National Register listings (public, non-restricted). crithab: USFWS critical habitat (final and proposed) at lon, lat. publiclands: USGS PAD-US 4.1 units with owners and access. elevation: USGS 3DEP EPQS at lon, lat. heritage: national heritage from four NPS services, one kind per call (kind=units | nha | battlefields | whs). units with bbox (at most 2 degrees, snapped to 0.25): NPS's authorised park unit boundaries, simplified to a thousandth of the box; units without bbox: every unit's centroid (437). nha: the 62 National Heritage Areas with NPS's description (shown as served, never embedded) and site link. battlefields with bbox (at most 8 degrees, snapped to 0.5): ABPP study areas and core areas of the Civil War, Revolutionary War and War of 1812 (PotNR and resurvey layers are left out), with `coverage` per layer. whs: World Heritage Sites with an NPS boundary, one feature per inscription. Designations, not ownership (PAD-US is /api/land?op=publiclands); battlefields are survey areas, mostly private land; no owner field is requested. tribal: BIA trust land (AIAN Land Area Representation), national.

get.summary: Slope, 2 ft contour, land cover and FEMA flood-map tiles rendered once and held at the edge; the hazard class, land cover class or slope at a point; the catalog of terrain pictures; Esri's Wayback release index; the USGS historical topographic maps at a point
get.description: op=tile: one 512 px PNG in Web Mercator (XYZ, y down) of a product no publisher caches as tiles: slope (USGS 3DEP "Slope Map", z 8-16), contours (3DEP "Preset 2ft Contour Interval", black lines on white, unlabelled, z 13-17), landcover (MRLC NLCD 2021 WMS, z 5-12), floodmap (FEMA NFHL layer 28 export, transparent, z 14-17). The route builds the upstream request from the product and the tile's EPSG:3857 box and never takes a URL; the image is the publisher's own render, cached a day in the server and for weeks at the edge. op=point: firehazard (USFS Wildfire Hazard Potential 2023 class, with the class table from the service's own legend), landcover (NLCD 2021 class, from MRLC's GetFeatureInfo and legend) or slope (3DEP "Slope Degrees", whole degrees) at lon, lat; a point with no value answers `class: null` / `degrees: null`, never 0. op=products: every terrain picture the globe draws, direct or rendered here, with its source, zoom range, class tables, caveats and the terrain tiles' required attribution. op=wayback: Esri World Imagery Wayback's release index, `releases` [{release, date}] newest first (2014-02-20 onward), parsed from each release's title (an undated entry is dropped, never guessed), held a day; the tile template with {release}; tiles are loaded from Esri by the browser and never proxied or cached here (the item's licence: not for offline tile export). A release date is when Esri published that basemap, not when its pixels were captured. op=topo: the USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection (1879-2006) at lon, lat (snapped to 0.01 degrees, held 30 days): `years` [{year, scales}] oldest first, the edition years with a sheet there (the years the map can draw there), and `sheets` newest edition first, each with its edition year (DateCurrent), scale, imprint and survey year (null when absent), USGS citation verbatim, and its GeoPDF and GeoTIFF from USGS TNM Access matched by scan id (null when TNM does not list the scan, or when TNM did not answer: the sheets still come back). A row with no edition year is dropped. `tiles` is the exportImage template with {year}; tiles load from Esri in the browser and draw only from about level 11. op=waybackdate: when the pixels of a Wayback release were captured at lon, lat, from that release's own imagery metadata service (its URL is read from Esri's index by release id, never taken from the caller; an id the index does not list is a 400; no release means the newest). z (0-23) picks the metadata band, layer 23 - z, and one neighbouring layer is tried when the rows' own MinMapLevel/MaxMapLevel miss z. Every row is returned (`captures`, oldest first: date from SRC_DATE, null when it does not parse; resolution and accuracy in metres; Esri's source code, collection name (a blank is null) and provider); no single row is picked, since rows tie on DrawOrder. Held 7 days per release, layer and point (0.001 degrees).

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: tile: a rendered PNG tile. point: a class or slope at lon, lat. products: the catalog. wayback: Esri World Imagery Wayback's release index. topo: the USGS historical topographic map editions and sheets at lon, lat. waybackdate: when a Wayback release's pixels were captured at lon, lat. naip: USDA NAIP aerial photograph years at a point (lon, lat; snapped to 0.001 degrees), from Microsoft Planetary Computer's STAC search: years [{ year, items: [{ id, date (acquisition, YYYY-MM-DD), gsd (m), state }] }], oldest first; none outside the conterminous US. naipmosaic: registers (or reuses, 24 h) Planetary Computer's mosaic for one year (year=yyyy, 2010 onward; a year the STAC search lists no NAIP item for is a 400, never registered) and answers { year, searchid, tiles (XYZ template on planetarycomputer.microsoft.com), minZoom 11 }; a held id is checked against Planetary Computer at most every 10 minutes and registered again when it is no longer known, at most once a year per 10 minutes (meta.reregisterCooling true while it waits); when the check fails the held id is served (meta.infoChecked false). Tiles load from Planetary Computer directly; below level 11 it answers no content.

parameters.description: op=waybackdate: a release id from op=wayback (the newest when absent). One Esri's index does not list is a 400.

parameters.description: op=tile: slope | contours | landcover | floodmap. op=point: firehazard | landcover | slope.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: op=tile: zoom, inside the product's range. op=waybackdate: the zoom level the imagery is drawn at (0-23), which picks Esri's metadata band (layer 23 - z).

parameters.description: op=tile: tile column.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: op=tile: tile row (XYZ, north at 0).

A component NRCS did not rate has `nccpi: null` and "Not rated", never 0. A soil rating, never a price or a parcel score.

parameters.description: op=point: longitude.

get.summary: The parcel at a point as its county or state publishes it, or parcel outlines in a small box
get.description: mode=identify (the default): the county at lon, lat (Census TIGERweb), the keyless parcel service wired for it, and the parcel record(s) there as that service publishes them: parcel id, site address, owner names (or `withheld` with the reason: the source's confidentiality flag, a placeholder such as "Current Owner", or New Jersey's Daniel's Law; or `not-published` where the service carries no owner field), mailing address, values each with the source's own label and year, exemption, use, zoning, year built, area with its basis, last sale, legal description, and the source's own record link. Also USDOT NAD address points on the parcel (`addresses`, null when NAD did not answer within 2.5 s) and, in the 30 PLSS states, the BLM township and section (`plss`). mode=outlines: parcel outlines in a box of at most 0.01° snapped to 0.002°, carrying the parcel id and use class only, never an owner. mode=addresses: NAD address points on the parcel at the point, waiting up to 30 s. There is no name parameter: `owner`, `name`, `q`, `where`, `search` and `query` are refused with 400.

get.description: op=point: the district a city's own zoning GIS puts the point in, with the city's description and category words, overlays and special districts, ordinance, effective date, case number and code link where the city publishes them. `state` is one of district, right-of-way (San Antonio's UZROW), no-district (no polygon at the point: a street, water or a gap; never 'unzoned'), no-ordinance (Houston) or not-covered (no source wired for the Census place under the point). New York adds the Zoning Tax Lot Database row of the tax lot under the point (MapPLUTO is asked for the BBL only), or DCP's overlay layers at the point where the lot has no row (condominium billing lots) or there is no lot; `overlaysUnknown` is true when neither answered. op=districts: district outlines (code and colour family only) from every covered city the box meets, generalised on each city's server to about 3 m; boxes clamped to 0.04° and snapped to 0.0025°. op=coverage: the cities, what each answers and why. Zoning as each city's GIS publishes it; the adopted zoning map and code govern.

get.summary: Building permits, business licences, environmental permits or EPA contaminated-site listings in a box; a TRI facility's reported releases
get.description: op=tri: what one Toxics Release Inventory facility reported releasing on site in a reporting year, from EPA Envirofacts (the Form R join of tri_reporting_form, tri_release_qty and tri_chem_info, and the facility's Form A certifications): `rows` by chemical and medium with the amount in its reported unit (null when 'NA' was entered or when it is a range report, which shows its range instead; a reported 0 stays 0), the estimation basis; `totals` per medium AND unit (pounds and grams are never added; range and NA rows are never in a total); `formA` the chemicals certified on Form A, which reports no quantities (null when that call failed). Fields are kept by allowlist: the certifying official and every contact name, phone and email Envirofacts sends never leave the parser, and TRI's own coordinates are not used. Held 30 days per facility and year. op=building: permits the cities list as issued in the last `days` (7-90, default 30), newest first, at most 500 per city; boxes clamped to 0.03° and snapped to 0.0025°. Each record keeps its valuation under the column it came from (reported cost, estimated project cost, valuation...), the parcel key the city publishes (BBL, TCAD id, SCHEDNUM, PIN, block/lot), the zoning printed on the permit where there is one, the contractor company and the city's record link. Every portal is asked for named columns ($select or outFields), and no applicant, owner or contact name is requested; the contractor company is shown as the city publishes it and can be a sole trader's own name (never searched). op=licences: licensed premises, by trade name (an entity's legal name where there is no trade name; the legal or registrant name is requested only to test for an entity form and to compare it with the trade name, and is discarded otherwise, so a trade name that is a non-company registrant's own name is not shown and `nameNote` says why; a trade name is otherwise as published and can contain a person's name), and licences at apartment or unit addresses withheld as a home-business heuristic (`withheld` counts them); boxes clamped to 0.02°. op=environmental: EPA ECHO NPDES and air facilities (compliance in ECHO's own words; 'not reported by ECHO' when it gives none) and the Corps' regulatory actions (the applicant is never kept; a project name that opens 'Surname, Given' is withheld and `facilityNote` says so, though a project name can carry a person's name in another form; the search returns at most 300, the box's actions first and then actions from anywhere in the country, so only those inside the box are kept, sorted newest first here, and USACE is partial only when all 300 lay in the box); boxes clamped to 0.2° and snapped to 0.05°. op=contaminants: EPA Envirofacts EMEF program listings, Superfund (EPA's SEMS site layer: the current National Priorities List, final and proposed sites, each with its NPL status and dates joined from EPA's NPL list by EPA ID; with polygons=1, EPA's Superfund site boundaries too, coloured by NPL status), Toxics Release Inventory reporters, RCRA hazardous-waste handlers and Brownfields (ACRES), as features named by their program id, with EPA's facility name (as published; it can be a person's name or a street address and is never a search key), the program id, the FRS registry id and EPA's record link in `details`; a listing is a regulatory status, not a finding of contamination, and no release amounts are given; no address is requested; at most 1,000 per program (`coverage` says partial when hit); same box rules as environmental. `coverage` lists every source the box meets with its state: covered, partial (a cap was hit), stale (Dallas), no-feed (Houston), token-required (Denver commercial), not-wired (San Antonio) or error (did not answer this time: missing, not absent).

parameters.name: trifid
parameters.description: op=tri: the TRI facility id (TRIFID), e.g. 77012HLLPT9701M; a TRI listing's program system id in op=contaminants.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: op=tri: reporting year, 1987 to this year. When absent, the newest complete year (two behind the calendar), then the one before if that holds nothing.

parameters.name: polygons
parameters.description: op=contaminants: also send polygons (EPA's Superfund site boundaries, USACE FUDS property boundaries and munitions response sites). The globe asks below 10 km; without it only points are sent.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: op=building: the window of issue dates.

get.summary: Community indicators by county and tract (CDC PLACES health estimates, CDC/ATSDR SVI), public schools (NCES), fixed broadband availability (FCC BDC via Esri) and housing assistance (HUD vouchers by tract, Qualified Census Tracts)
get.description: op=health: CDC PLACES, 2025 release (data year 2023; 2022 for five measures), model-based estimates for 40 measures. level=county&measure=: every county's age-adjusted prevalence for one measure from one whole-measure pull (held a week), with national quintile `breaks`; join by `fips` onto county outlines (Connecticut in planning regions). level=tract&measure=&counties=: crude prevalence for every published tract of at most 6 counties, asked by countyfips (never within_box). level=place&fips=: every measure for one county, age-adjusted. A county or tract with no row is not published, never 0. Estimates, not counts of diagnosed people; not for ranking small differences. op=svi: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022 (ACS 2018-2022). level=county: every county's overall percentile (RPL_THEMES) and four theme percentiles (Socioeconomic Status, Household Characteristics, Racial and Ethnic Minority Status, Housing Type and Transportation) and F_TOTAL, attributes only, as compact rows { fips, name, state, rpl: [overall, theme1..theme4], flags } (held a week); join by `fips` onto county outlines (Connecticut in planning regions). level=tract&bbox=: SVI's own tract polygons (GeoJSON, simplified to 0.0005 degrees) in a box of at most 0.4 degrees snapped to 0.05, at most two pages of 2,000. level=place&fips=: one county (5 digits) or tract (11 digits) with the 16 estimates (EP_) and margins (MP_); 404 when CDC has no row. CDC's -999 ('not ranked': 778 tracts, 0 counties on 2026-10-16) is null at level=county and level=place (rankings, flags, estimates and margins), never 0; level=tract passes CDC's properties through as published, so an unranked tract carries the raw -999 in every RPL_ field and F_TOTAL: not ranked, never least vulnerable. A percentile among US counties (or tracts), 0 least to 1 most vulnerable; not FEMA's NRI social vulnerability (/api/hazards?op=nri, from the Census Community Resilience Estimate), and the two are never merged. op=schools&bbox=: NCES EDGE public schools, school year 2024-25 (EDGE_ADMINDATA_PUBLICSCH_2425), as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of points in a box of at most 0.2 degrees (snapped to 0.05), at most two pages of 2,000, held a day: directory fields, enrollment (TOTAL), free or reduced-price lunch (TOTFRL), FTE and STUTERATIO as NCES publishes them; no race, sex or grade-level enrollment cell is requested. A negative is a CCD reporting code (-1 not reported, -2 not applicable), never 0. Inactive and Future schools are left out and counted in `hidden`. op=broadband: FCC Broadband Data Collection, December 2025, as Esri Policy Maps summarizes it (the summary layer is under the Esri Master License Agreement; the figures are the FCC's). level=county: every county's Broadband Serviceable Location counts as compact arrays, `columns` = [geoid, total, unserved, underserved, served, fiber, cable, ltfw, providers, unserved12] (two pages of 2,000, held a week); join by `geoid` onto county outlines. Connecticut is published only in its eight legacy counties (09001-09015), listed in meta.unmatched and never crosswalked; its planning regions have no row. level=hex&bbox=: BDC's own H3 resolution-8 hexagons (GeoJSON) in a box of at most 0.3 degrees snapped to 0.05, one page of 2,000; counts as published, including single-location hexagons. level=place&fips=: one county with every technology column, providers, Esri's 6- and 12-month-previous counts, and shares[] as named ratios of two published counts (null where TotalBSLs is 0); 404 when BDC has no row. Served, underserved and unserved are the FCC tiers by speed and technology; satellite and unlicensed fixed wireless count as unserved. Availability as providers report it: not subscription, not measured speed. op=housing: HUD's Housing Choice Vouchers by tract (GEOID, HCV_PUBLIC voucher households, HCV_PUBLIC_PCT HUD's share of 2020 Census renter-occupied units) and HUD's Qualified Census Tracts titled 2026 (GEOID), each on its own 2020 tract polygons; bbox=: a box of at most 0.3 degrees snapped to 0.05, one page of 2,000 each, as data { hcv, qct } FeatureCollections, held a week per box; only those named fields are read (never *). HCV_PUBLIC is null where HUD omits tracts with 10 or fewer voucher holders (47,463 of 85,154 tracts), never 0; every Connecticut tract (881, filed under the legacy counties) is null, which is 'not published', not suppression. QCT Connecticut tracts use planning-region codes. HUD titles the QCT list 2026; its item snippet says 2025 and its layer description 2024. level=place&fips=<11-digit tract>: { geoid, vouchers, share, status (published, suppressed, not-published-ct, not-in-layer), qct (true, false, or null: unknown for a Connecticut legacy-county tract code, which the planning-region QCT list never uses) }; 404 when neither layer has the tract. Round 8: part=dda, part=lihtc or part=dda,lihtc (with bbox) add data.dda, HUD's Difficult Development Areas titled 2026 (ZCTA5, DDA_CODE, DDA_TYPE SA metro ZCTA or NM non-metro county, DDA_NAME; the layer's own text says 2023-2024), and data.lihtc, HUD's LIHTC properties (HUD_ID, PROJECT, PROJ_ADD, PROJ_CTY, PROJ_ST, PROJ_ZIP, N_UNITS, LI_UNITS, YR_PIS, YR_ALLOC, NON_PROF, CREDIT, TYPE, TRGT_POP, BOND, DDA, QCT, CURCNTY, LVL2KX), in the same box and page. The owner and contact block (CONTACT, COMPANY, CO_*) is never requested. LIHTC is asked where N_UNITS >= 5: a project of fewer than five units (a household's home) never reaches the server and is never counted in an answer. Coded LIHTC fields are HUD's codes (HUD's data dictionary could not be read keyless); 8888 and 9999 in YR_PIS and YR_ALLOC are codes, not years. The globe draws only LVL2KX R and 4, as HUD's layer description asks. part=hcv or part=qct is a 400: they are the default.
